record: As Oversight chairman, opened an investigation into Delaware's Artificial Intelligence Company proposal, asking for the state's assessment of its risks.
Chaired the full-committee hearing 'The Federal Government in the Age of Artificial Intelligence' on federal AI adoption.
grade_reason: Comer has spoken about AI in 2026 (the Delaware AI-company investigation) and 2025, but only about liability, consumer harm, government adoption and competitiveness; no statement acknowledging catastrophic AI risk was found.
notes: All 6 required web searches ran this time, plus 1 extra search on Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act cosponsors (7 in total). None of the searches found any statement by Comer about superintelligence, extinction, existential risk, loss of control, a pause, slowdown or moratorium on AI development, or an AI agreement with China. Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act: the House version (listed by fastdemocracy.com as H.R. 10538, introduced September 2026) was referred to the Oversight Committee, which Comer chairs; cosponsor lists seen (Hoyle, Lynch, Tonko; or Ocasio-Cortez plus other Democrats per Forkast) do not include Comer, and no source shows him sponsoring or co-sponsoring it. Congress.gov cosponsor list was not opened. Delaware AI-company investigation (2026-10-26): the press release was reopened and its quote rechecked; the letter also says Delaware's commission did not assess 'potential safety, harms, risks', but no catastrophic harm or loss of control is named, so it stays D. A secondary report says the letter describes AI agents engaging in 'any business activity'; not verified against the original letter and not used. Comer and Timmons' 2026 investigations into national security risks of US-China science and technology research sharing (oversight.house.gov, April and June 2026) are about research security, not AI risk, and are left out. comer.house.gov itself is not in the search index; earlier direct checks of its site search found no AI-related releases since 2025. The 5 June 2025 hearing transcript (govinfo CHRG-119hhrg60818) contains no mention of extinction, superintelligence, existential risk, loss of control or bioweapons. Comer and Raskin's Federal AI Governance and Transparency Act (H.R. 7532) dates from March 2024, before the period covered, so it is left out. Oversight Committee releases are issued by Comer as chairman; quotes are attributed to him by name. Large House letters were not searched, per instructions.
